t: A Wolof-led confederation in Senegambia, uniting Waalo, Cayor, Baol, Sine and Saloum under an overlord called the buurba.
It linked the interior with the Atlantic coast just as Portuguese traders arrived, and spread Wolof language across the region.
Atlantic wealth let coastal vassals break away; Cayor's victory at Danki c. 1549 ended Jolof's imperial phase.
dyk: In 1488 the exiled Jolof prince Bemoim was received and baptised at the court of King Joao II in Lisbon.
ev: Ndiadiane Ndiaye, by tradition, draws the Wolof and Serer states into the Jolof confederation
Venetian Alvise Cadamosto sees Portuguese traders exchanging horses for slaves on the Senegal coast
Exiled Jolof prince Bemoim is baptised at the court of Joao II in Lisbon
Amari Ngone Sobel Fall of Cayor defeats and kills the buurba Leele Fuli Fak at Danki
The rump kingdom of Jolof is absorbed into French Senegal
